X.note: The environment is strong: the weathered walls, raking light, shutters and rubble, and the flag at the vanishing point give a good lead-in. The figures are flat, doll-like, stiff-armed and sparse, with a mostly bare-headed, uniform-red look. Some have a bare, cut-out torso and one has an odd dark cloak. The flag is the Union Jack with the 1801 Irish cross, which is too early for 1782. The group is small and spaced out, so the lane stays readable and uncluttered.

Y.note: The environment is identical. Y adds a larger crowd and two big foreground figures in blue coats with white crossbelts, so the lane reads as busier and more populated. The foreground figures have stiff, mannequin-like poses, plastic-looking faces and uniform proportions. The crowd in the middle distance is a cluster of near-identical clones with muddled overlap. The crossbelts and red/blue facings are more varied than in X, but the same flag problem applies. The larger figures expose the game-asset quality more.

why: The environment is identical, but X's fewer, smaller figures keep the toy-like look less exposed and the lane readable, while Y's large mannequin-like foreground figures and cloned crowd make the game-asset look worse.
top_fix_for_weaker: Remove or push back the two large foreground figures and thin the cloned crowd. Vary poses, heights, headgear and uniform wear, add motion blur or haze and contact shadows, and replace the flag with the pre-1801 Union flag (St George and St Andrew crosses only).
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack with the St Patrick's cross (post-1801) on the flag
Possible 19th-century shako-like headgear on some figures
Uniformly clean modern-looking tunics for a besieged garrison
